summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP on install and import
details: Package in the internal-looking @ecg-internal scope ships a postinstall script and a main-entry side effect that both execute beacon.cjs, which POSTs the installer's hostname (require('os').hostname()), __dirname, process.cwd(), and process.version to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc over plain HTTP. The beacon fires automatically on `npm install` (scripts.postinstall = "node beacon.cjs") and again whenever the module is required. The main export is a Proxy that returns no-op functions for any property access, allowing a consumer bundler that imports the impersonated internal package to continue past the import while the beacon has already executed. The combination of an internal-looking scope, a trivial Proxy shim designed to not break the victim build, and automatic install/import-time egress of host identifiers to an attacker-controlled bare-IP collector is the dependency-confusion payload shape. The README self-describes as an authorized test, but the code behavior itself exfiltrates installer host data to a hardcoded third-party endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
